privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: ONE was designed with "privacy by design" in mind: the vast majority of operations — merging, compressing, converting, editing PDFs, images, audio or video — run entirely inside your browser, on your own device. Your files are never sent to a server. This policy explains precisely what data is nonetheless processed, why, and what your rights are.

sections.heading: 1. Data controller
sections.body: The data controller within the meaning of the GDPR is [TO BE COMPLETED — official name of the publisher (full name, or company name + legal form + registration number)], reachable at [TO BE COMPLETED — dedicated contact email address, e.g. contact@yourdomain.com]. See the Legal Notice for the publisher’s full identification.

sections.heading: 2. Core principle: your files stay with you
sections.body:
The document, image, audio and video tools offered by ONE run exclusively on the client side, using browser technologies (WebAssembly, Web Workers, File API). Specifically:
- The file you import is never uploaded to a publisher server.
- No copy of your file, or of its content, is retained by the publisher, in any form whatsoever.
- Processing (merging, compression, OCR, conversion, etc.) happens in memory, inside your browser tab, and the result is offered for download directly from your device.

This local-processing approach is core to how the Service works and is not a switchable option.

sections.heading: 3. Data we actually collect
sections.body:
Consistent with the data-minimization principle (GDPR art. 5.1.c), we only collect what is strictly necessary for the Service to function:
- Data stored locally in your browser (localStorage), which never leaves your device: theme preference (light/dark), chosen language, a history of your last 20 operations (tool used, file name, timestamp — never the file content), and your choice regarding the cookie banner.
- Standard technical connection data collected by our host (Vercel) to provide the Service and secure the infrastructure: IP address, browser type, pages visited, request timestamps. These server logs are managed by the host under its own policy and are not used by the publisher for commercial purposes.
- If you create an account (optional feature): your name, email address and a session identifier, stored only in your browser's local storage — never sent to a server, never synced across devices or browsers. Your password is never stored in clear text: only its SHA-256 hash is kept locally.

We do not collect or infer any sensitive data or precise geolocation data, and we do not use any third-party audience-analytics tool (no Google Analytics or equivalent) or targeted advertising as of the date of this policy.

sections.heading: 4. Purposes of processing
5. Legal basis for processing
6. Recipients of data
7. Transfers outside your country of residence
sections.body: Our host operates a global infrastructure that may involve processing of technical connection logs in the United States or other countries where Vercel operates servers. To the extent this involves personal data of EU residents, such transfer relies on appropriate safeguards under the GDPR (standard contractual clauses or an equivalent mechanism recognized by the European Commission). Your files themselves are never transferred anywhere, since they are never sent to a server.

sections.heading: 8. Retention period
sections.body: Files you process are never retained: they exist only in your browser’s working memory for the duration of processing, then are cleared when the tab or browser is closed. Preference data and local history stay on your device until you delete them yourself (Settings page, "Clear history" button) or clear your browser’s browsing data; local history is additionally auto-capped at the 20 most recent operations. The host’s technical connection logs are kept for the standard duration applied by Vercel for operating and securing its infrastructure.

sections.heading: 9. Data security
sections.body: The architectural choice of 100% local processing inherently reduces your data’s exposure: since no file is ever sent to a server, there is no database containing your documents that could be breached or leaked. The Service is also served exclusively over HTTPS (encrypted transport). Local storage (localStorage) remains subject to your own browser’s and device’s security mechanisms: we recommend keeping your browser up to date and securing physical access to your device.

sections.heading: 10. Your rights
11. Minors
sections.body: The Service is not specifically directed at minors and does not knowingly target children for data collection. If you believe a minor has provided us with personal data without the required consent, please contact us so we can delete it.

sections.heading: 12. Cookies and similar technologies

cookiePolicy.title: Cookie Policy
cookiePolicy.intro: This policy explains what cookies and local-storage technologies are, which ones ONE uses, why, and how you can manage them. It complements our Privacy Policy.

sections.heading: 1. What are cookies and local storage?
sections.body: A "cookie" is a small text file placed by a website on your device. "Local storage" (localStorage) is a similar, more modern technology that lets a website store information directly in your browser, with no automatic expiry date. ONE does not use classic tracking cookies but relies on browser local storage, which is subject to the same regulatory framework (ePrivacy Directive / GDPR).

sections.heading: 2. What we do not use
3. What is stored locally on your device
sections.body:
The only items stored in your browser’s local storage are:
- one-theme — remembers your light/dark display preference. Strictly necessary for the interface to work as expected; no consent required.
- one-language — remembers your chosen language. Strictly necessary; no consent required.
- one-history — remembers your last 20 operations (tool name, file name, date), for the "History" feature you requested. Functional, on by default because it is a service you explicitly requested; you can clear it at any time from Settings.
- one-cookie-consent — remembers the choice you made through the consent banner, so it is not shown again on every visit.

sections.heading: 4. Legal basis and consent
sections.body: Items strictly necessary for the Service to work (theme, language) are exempt from prior consent under ePrivacy regulation. Local history, while not indispensable to displaying the Service, corresponds to a feature explicitly requested by the user when opening the History panel; we nonetheless collect your overall choice through the consent banner for the sake of transparency, and you can disable it at any time by clearing your history from Settings.

sections.heading: 5. How to manage your preferences
6. Retention period
sections.body: Local storage data has no automatic expiry: it stays on your device until you delete it manually or clear your browsing data. Local history is additionally auto-capped at the 20 most recent operations.

sections.heading: 7. Changes to this policy
sections.body: This cookie policy may be updated if the technologies used by the Service evolve (for example, the future addition of an audience-analytics tool). Any significant change will trigger a new consent request where applicable.
